metadata.title: Shannon Shakes Hands with Chernoff: Big Data Viewpoint On Channel Information Measures

extraction_notes.note: The main findings are read off ACE-transform plots (figures); stated as claims with rigor numerical.
The ACE pseudocode prints the 'Iterate until' line twice (outer and inner loop) and closes loops with plain STATE lines; the two End-loop lines were dropped and the steps left flat as returned.
corollary or claim: the paper itself calls this inference 'this corollary', so corollary was kept.
Descriptions of the simulated data sets (20000/60000 observations) and the km/cm analogy were left as discussion, not nodes.

nodes.name: Channel capacity
nodes.statement: As a matter of fact, the channel capacity is defined as maximization mutual information.
also_stated_at: For example, the maximum mutual information is defined as the channel capacity for a discrete memoryless channel.

nodes.name: Shannon mutual information
nodes.statement: According to [\cite{Elements}], the Shannon mutual information is defined as: \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} & I_S(X,Y) = D(p(x,y)||p(x)p(y)) \cr & = \sum\limits_{x,y} {p(x,y)log{{p(x,y)} \over {p(x)p(y)}}} \cr \end{aligned} \end{equation} where $X,Y$ are two random variables with marginal probability mass functions $p(x)$ and $p(y)$ and joint probability mass function $p(x,y)$.
nodes.origin_citation: Cover & Thomas, Elements of Information Theory
nodes.statement_short: Shannon mutual information as the KL divergence between the joint pmf and the product of marginals.

nodes.name: Shannon mutual information formula
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} & I_S(X,Y) = D(p(x,y)||p(x)p(y)) \cr & = \sum\limits_{x,y} {p(x,y)log{{p(x,y)} \over {p(x)p(y)}}} \cr \end{aligned}
nodes.origin_citation: Cover & Thomas, Elements of Information Theory
nodes.label: Shannon Information

nodes.name: Relative entropy (Kullback-Leibler distance)
nodes.statement: The relative entropy is given by [\cite{Elements}]: \begin{equation} D(p||q) = \sum\limits_{x \in \textit{X}} {p(x)log{{p(x)} \over {q(x)}}} \end{equation}
nodes.origin_citation: Cover & Thomas, Elements of Information Theory

nodes.name: Relative entropy formula
nodes.statement: D(p||q) = \sum\limits_{x \in \textit{X}} {p(x)log{{p(x)} \over {q(x)}}}
nodes.origin_citation: Cover & Thomas, Elements of Information Theory
nodes.label: KL distance

nodes.name: Chernoff information
nodes.statement: As defined in [\cite{Elements}], it is given by \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} I_C({{\rm{P}}_1},{P_2}) \buildrel \Delta \over = - \mathop {\min }\limits_{0 \le \alpha \le 1} \log \left( {\sum\limits_x {P_1^\alpha (x)P_2^{1 - \alpha }(x)} } \right) \end{aligned} \end{equation} where $\alpha$ is real parameter with $0\leq \alpha \leq 1$.
nodes.origin_citation: Cover & Thomas, Elements of Information Theory
nodes.statement_short: Chernoff information of two distributions: minus the minimum over $\alpha\in[0,1]$ of the log of $\sum P_1^\alpha P_2^{1-\alpha}$.

nodes.name: Chernoff information formula
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} I_C({{\rm{P}}_1},{P_2}) \buildrel \Delta \over = - \mathop {\min }\limits_{0 \le \alpha \le 1} \log \left( {\sum\limits_x {P_1^\alpha (x)P_2^{1 - \alpha }(x)} } \right) \end{aligned}
nodes.origin_citation: Cover & Thomas, Elements of Information Theory
nodes.label: Chernoff Information1

nodes.name: Chernoff mutual information
nodes.statement: With the aid of Chernoff information to describe the relationship between the two variables, a new mutual information is defined as \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} I_C(X,Y) \buildrel \Delta \over = - \mathop {\min }\limits_{0 \le \alpha \le 1} \log \left( {\sum\limits_x {\sum\limits_y {{p^\alpha }(x,y){{(p(x)p(y))}^{1 - \alpha }}} } } \right). \end{aligned} \end{equation} In this paper, we call it Chernoff mutual information relative to Shannon mutual information.
nodes.statement_short: Chernoff mutual information: Chernoff information between the joint pmf and the product of marginals.

nodes.name: Chernoff mutual information formula
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} I_C(X,Y) \buildrel \Delta \over = - \mathop {\min }\limits_{0 \le \alpha \le 1} \log \left( {\sum\limits_x {\sum\limits_y {{p^\alpha }(x,y){{(p(x)p(y))}^{1 - \alpha }}} } } \right). \end{aligned}
nodes.label: Chernoff Information2

nodes.name: Binary symmetric channel (BSC)
nodes.statement: Consider the BSC, which is shown in Fig.\ref{fig:channelBSC}. It is a binary channel where the probability of the input symbols is $(\lambda,1-\lambda)$.
differentia: the probability of the input symbols is $(\lambda,1-\lambda)$

nodes.name: BSC transmission error
nodes.statement: The transmission error in it is $\varepsilon $.

nodes.name: Shannon mutual information of the BSC
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} & I_S(X;Y) = H(Y) - H(Y|X) \cr & = \sum\limits_{k = 1}^2 {\sum\limits_{j = 1}^2 {p({x_k},{y_j})log{{p({x_k},{y_j})} \over {p({x_k})p({y_j})}}} } \cr & = (1 - \varepsilon )\log {{1 - \varepsilon } \over {\lambda (1 - \varepsilon ) + (1 - \lambda )\varepsilon }} + \varepsilon \log {\varepsilon \over {\lambda \varepsilon + (1 - \lambda )(1 - \varepsilon )}}. \cr \end{aligned}
nodes.label: BSC Mutual information

nodes.name: Chernoff mutual information of the BSC
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &I_C(X;Y)=- \mathop {\min }\limits_{0 \le \alpha \le 1} \log \left( {\sum\limits_x {P_1^\alpha (x)P_2^{1 - \alpha }(x)} } \right)\\ &=- \mathop {\min }\limits_{0 \le \alpha \le 1} \log ( {(1 - \varepsilon )^\alpha }{\left( {\lambda (1 - \varepsilon ) + (1 - \lambda )\varepsilon } \right)^{1 - \alpha }} \\ &+ {\varepsilon ^\alpha }{\left( {\lambda \varepsilon + (1 - \lambda )(1 - \varepsilon )} \right)^{1 - \alpha }} ) \end{aligned}
nodes.label: BSC Chernoff information

nodes.name: No explicit solution for BSC Chernoff mutual information
nodes.statement: Unfortunately, there is no explicit solution for Eq.(\ref{BSC Chernoff information}). As a result, it is arduous to analyze the Chernoff mutual information.

nodes.name: Multiple symmetric channel (MSC)
nodes.statement: The MSC is shown in Fig.\ref{fig:channelMBSC}. The number of input symbol is $M$.

nodes.name: MSC input probabilities
nodes.statement: The probability of the input symbol is $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,...,\lambda_M)$ with $\lambda_1+\lambda_2+...+\lambda_M=1$ ($\lambda_i>0$).

nodes.name: MSC transmission error
nodes.statement: The transmission error of each one is $\frac{\varepsilon}{M-1}$.

nodes.name: BSC is the special case of MSC
nodes.statement: The BSC is the special case of MSC for $M=2$.

nodes.name: Shannon mutual information of the MSC
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} & I_S(X;Y) = D(p(x,y)||p(x)p(y)) \cr & = \sum\limits_{k = 1}^M {\sum\limits_{j = 1}^M {p({x_k},{y_j})log{{p({x_k},{y_j})} \over {p({x_k})p({y_j})}}} } \cr \end{aligned}
nodes.label: MSC Mutual information

nodes.name: Chernoff mutual information of the MSC
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &I_C(X;Y)=- \mathop {\min }\limits_{0 \le \alpha \le 1} \log \left( {\sum\limits_x {{p(xy)}^\alpha (x){(p(x)p(y))}^{1 - \alpha }(x)} } \right)\\ \end{aligned}
nodes.label: MSC Chernoff information

nodes.name: Predictors and response
nodes.statement: Assume random variables $X_1,X_2,\cdots ,X_p$ are predictors and $Y$ is response.

nodes.name: ACE residual error
nodes.statement: Supposing $\phi _1(X_1),\phi _2(X_2),\cdots,\phi _p(X_p),\theta (Y)$ are arbitrary zero mean functions of the corresponding variables, the residual error is \begin{equation} {e^2}\left( {\theta ,{\phi _1},\cdots,{\phi _p}} \right) = {{E\left\{ {{{\left[ {\theta (Y) - \sum\limits_{i = 1}^p {{\phi _i}({X_i})} } \right]}^2}} \right\}} \over {E\left[ {{\theta ^2}(Y)} \right]}} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Normalized squared residual of $\theta(Y)$ against the sum of zero-mean transforms $\phi_i(X_i)$.

nodes.name: ACE residual error formula
nodes.statement: {e^2}\left( {\theta ,{\phi _1},\cdots,{\phi _p}} \right) = {{E\left\{ {{{\left[ {\theta (Y) - \sum\limits_{i = 1}^p {{\phi _i}({X_i})} } \right]}^2}} \right\}} \over {E\left[ {{\theta ^2}(Y)} \right]}}

nodes.name: ACE Algorithm (alternating conditional expectation)
nodes.statement: \caption{ACE Algorithm} \begin{algorithmic}[1] \STATE set $\theta (Y) = Y/\left\| Y \right\|$ and ${\phi _1}({X_1}),...,{\phi _p}({X_p}) = 0$;\\ \STATE Iterate until $e^2(\theta,\phi_1,...,\phi_p)$fails to decrease;\\ \STATE Iterate until $e^2(\theta,\phi_1,...,\phi_p)$fails to decrease;\\ \STATE For $k=1$ to p Do:\\ \begin{equation*} {\phi _{k,1}}({X_k}) = E\left[ {\theta (Y) - \sum\limits_{i \ne k} {{\phi _i}\left( {{X_i}} \right)} \left| {{X_k}} \right.} \right]; \end{equation*} replace $\phi_k(X_k)$ with $\phi_{k,1}(X_k)$;\\ End For Loop;\\ \STATE End Inner Iteration Loop;\\ \STATE \begin{equation*} {\theta _1}(Y) = {{E\left[ {\sum\limits_{i = 1} {{\phi _i}({X_i})\left| Y \right.} } \right]} \over {\left\| {E\left[ {\sum\limits_{i = 1}^p {{\phi _i}({X_i})\left| Y \right.} } \right]} \right\|}}; \end{equation*} replace $\theta(Y)$ with $\theta_1(Y)$;\\ \STATE End Outer Iteration Loop;\\ \STATE $\theta,\phi_1,...,\phi_p$ are the solution $\theta^*,\phi^*_1,...,\phi^*_p$;\\ \end{algorithmic}
nodes.statement_short: Alternating conditional expectations: iteratively replace each $\phi_k$ and $\theta$ by conditional expectations until $e^2$ stops decreasing.
nodes.label: alg:ACE

nodes.name: Initialize transforms
nodes.statement: set $\theta (Y) = Y/\left\| Y \right\|$ and ${\phi _1}({X_1}),...,{\phi _p}({X_p}) = 0$;
nodes.statement_short: Normalize $\theta(Y)$ and set all $\phi_i$ to zero.

nodes.name: Outer iteration
nodes.statement: Iterate until $e^2(\theta,\phi_1,...,\phi_p)$fails to decrease;
nodes.statement_short: Outer loop until the residual error stops decreasing.

nodes.name: Inner iteration
nodes.statement: Iterate until $e^2(\theta,\phi_1,...,\phi_p)$fails to decrease;
nodes.statement_short: Inner loop until the residual error stops decreasing.

nodes.name: Update each predictor transform
nodes.statement_short: For each $k$, replace $\phi_k$ by the conditional expectation of the partial residual given $X_k$.

nodes.name: Update response transform
nodes.statement_short: Replace $\theta$ by the normalized conditional expectation of $\sum\phi_i$ given $Y$.

nodes.name: Return solution
nodes.statement: $\theta,\phi_1,...,\phi_p$ are the solution $\theta^*,\phi^*_1,...,\phi^*_p$;

nodes.name: Channel parameters and channel information value
nodes.statement: Let $X_1,X_2,\cdots,X_p$ be the channel parameters and $Y$ be measured value of channel information.

nodes.name: Functional relation f
nodes.statement: The functional relation between them is: \begin{equation} Y = f({X_1},{X_2},...,{X_p}). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Channel information as a function of channel parameters
nodes.label: Eq ACE Alg4

nodes.name: Channel parameters known and independent
nodes.statement: It is supposed that ${X_1},{X_2},...,{X_p}$ are known and independent.

nodes.name: Functional relation known
nodes.statement: Moreover, the functional relation $f$ is also known since it is defined by human to describe the channel information.

nodes.name: ACE decomposition and residual delta
nodes.statement: As a result, one can get \begin{equation} \theta (Y) = \sum\limits_{i = 1}^p {{\phi _i}(X_i)} + \delta \end{equation} where $\delta$ is residual error.
nodes.statement_short: ACE applied to the channel data yields $\theta(Y)=\sum_i\phi_i(X_i)+\delta$ with residual $\delta$.

nodes.name: ACE additive decomposition
nodes.statement: \theta (Y) = \sum\limits_{i = 1}^p {{\phi _i}(X_i)} + \delta
nodes.label: ACE_Def

nodes.name: Simulation Procedure
nodes.statement: \caption*{Simulation Procedure} \begin{algorithmic}[1] \STATE Generate channel parameters, such as $\lambda$ and $\varepsilon$; \STATE Calculate the channel information measures, such as Shannon mutual information; \STATE Decompose these channel information measures by ACE algorithm; \STATE Repeat above process till the required times. \end{algorithmic}
nodes.statement_short: Monte Carlo: sample channel parameters, compute information measures, decompose them with ACE, repeat.
nodes.label: alg:simulated

nodes.name: Generate channel parameters
nodes.statement: Generate channel parameters, such as $\lambda$ and $\varepsilon$;

nodes.name: Compute information measures
nodes.statement: Calculate the channel information measures, such as Shannon mutual information;

nodes.name: ACE decomposition
nodes.statement: Decompose these channel information measures by ACE algorithm;

nodes.name: Repeat
nodes.statement: Repeat above process till the required times.

nodes.name: BSC: ACE transforms coincide for Shannon and Chernoff
nodes.statement: It is noted that function curve of $\phi_1(\lambda)$ and $\phi_2(\varepsilon)$ w.r.t. Shannon mutual information is almost coincided with that w.r.t Chernoff mutual information after the ACE decomposition.
conclusions: function curve of $\phi_1(\lambda)$ and $\phi_2(\varepsilon)$ w.r.t. Shannon mutual information is almost coincided with that w.r.t Chernoff mutual information after the ACE decomposition

nodes.name: BSC: Shannon smaller than Chernoff with identical trend
nodes.statement: The results of Shannon mutual information are smaller than the Chernoff mutual information, but whole variant trend is identical.
conclusions: The results of Shannon mutual information are smaller than the Chernoff mutual information, but whole variant trend is identical

nodes.name: MSC: ACE transforms coincide for Shannon and Chernoff
nodes.statement: It is obviously that the function curves of $\theta(y)$,$\phi_1(\lambda_1)$,$\phi_2(\lambda_2)$,$\phi_3(\lambda_3)$ and $\phi_4(\varepsilon)$ are almost the same for these two channel information measures.
conclusions: the function curves of $\theta(y)$,$\phi_1(\lambda_1)$,$\phi_2(\lambda_2)$,$\phi_3(\lambda_3)$ and $\phi_4(\varepsilon)$ are almost the same for these two channel information measures

nodes.name: MSC: Shannon smaller than Chernoff with identical trend
nodes.statement: As illustrated in Fig.\ref{fig:MSC C and I}, the result of Shannon mutual information is smaller than the Chernoff mutual information, but whole varying trend is identical.
conclusions: the result of Shannon mutual information is smaller than the Chernoff mutual information, but whole varying trend is identical

nodes.name: ACE result form Y = psi(varphi(X))
nodes.statement: The ACE results is \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} Y = f\left( {\textbf{X}} \right) \overset{(a)}{=}{\theta ^{ - 1}}\left( {\sum\limits_{i = 1}^p {{\phi _i}({X_i})} } \right)= \psi \left( {\varphi \left( { {\textbf{X}} } \right)} \right)\\ \end{aligned} \end{equation} where $Y$ is the channel information and ${\textbf{X}}$ is all the set of all the input channel parameters.
nodes.statement_short: ACE expresses channel information as $Y=\theta^{-1}(\sum\phi_i(X_i))=\psi(\varphi(\mathbf X))$.

nodes.name: ACE result function
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} Y = f\left( {\textbf{X}} \right) \overset{(a)}{=}{\theta ^{ - 1}}\left( {\sum\limits_{i = 1}^p {{\phi _i}({X_i})} } \right)= \psi \left( {\varphi \left( { {\textbf{X}} } \right)} \right)\\ \end{aligned}
nodes.label: Res_Fun

nodes.name: phi_i identical for Shannon and Chernoff
nodes.statement: From the figures above, it is noted that $ \phi_i(X_i)$ is almost the same for both Shannon and Chernoff mutual information.
conclusions: $ \phi_i(X_i)$ is almost the same for both Shannon and Chernoff mutual information

nodes.name: Argument for Shannon's inverse transform being bigger
nodes.statement: As mentioned above, the curves of $\theta(\cdot)$ have the same trend and the values of $\theta(Y)$ for Shannon mutual information is invariably smaller than those for Chernoff information.
nodes.statement_short: Since $\theta$ is monotonic and Shannon's $\theta(Y)$ lies below Chernoff's, invert the comparison.

nodes.name: Shannon's inverse theta bigger than Chernoff's
nodes.statement: Therefore, the Shannon's $\theta^{-1}(\cdot)$ is bigger than Chernoff's.
conclusions: the Shannon's $\theta^{-1}(\cdot)$ is bigger than Chernoff's

nodes.name: KL divergence is the special case of Renyi divergence at alpha=1
nodes.statement: Over the last decades, Shannon information and Chernoff information are always considered to be two kinds of channel information measures and the relation between them is that Kullback-Leibler divergence is the special case of R{\'{e}}nyi divergence when $\alpha=1$.
conclusions: Kullback-Leibler divergence is the special case of R{\'{e}}nyi divergence when $\alpha=1$

nodes.name: Physical argument for consistency of channel information
nodes.statement: For a channel, in a certain time, if all of its parameters are given, all of its state and properties will be determined. Thus the information about the same channel is always consistent.
nodes.statement_short: Physical argument: a channel's parameters determine its state, so all information about it is consistent.

nodes.name: Shannon and Chernoff measure the same physical quantity
nodes.statement: In fact, they are different metrics of the same physical quantity.
conclusions: they are different metrics of the same physical quantity
also_stated_at: Similarly, the Shannon and Chernoff information are two metrics of the same quantity of information.

nodes.name: Nature of channel information
nodes.statement: In this paper, we take $\varphi \left( {\textbf{X}}\right)$ as the nature of channel information and we get \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \varPsi=\varphi \left( {\textbf{X}} \right) \end{aligned} \end{equation} where the $\varPsi$ is the nature of channel information.

nodes.name: Nature of channel information
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \varPsi=\varphi \left( {\textbf{X}} \right) \end{aligned}
nodes.label: Nature_Fun

nodes.name: Channel information measures are functions of Psi
nodes.statement: The other physical quantity about channel information is just the function of $\varPsi$, just as \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \rm{I}= \psi (\varPsi) \end{aligned} \end{equation} where $\rm{I}$ is a measurement of channel information.
conclusions: The other physical quantity about channel information is just the function of $\varPsi$

nodes.name: Information measure as function of nature
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \rm{I}= \psi (\varPsi) \end{aligned}
nodes.label: Nature_Fun1

nodes.name: Nature-of-channel-information conjecture
nodes.statement: There is a conjecture that if a novel information measure is put forward to measure the channel information, it will be decomposed to a function of $\psi(\cdot)$ by ACE algorithm from a very large extent.
assumptions: a novel information measure is put forward to measure the channel information
conclusions: it will be decomposed to a function of $\psi(\cdot)$ by ACE algorithm from a very large extent
nodes.statement_short: Any new channel information measure decomposes by ACE as some $\psi$ of the same nature $\varPsi$.
